newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi sees Iraqi oil having limited market impact.
newsitem.headline: Saudi sees Iraqi oil having limited market impact.

text.p: Iraqi oil exports has only a limited impact on the international oil market, Saudi Oil Minister Ali bin Ibrahim al-Nuaimi was quoted as saying by the official Saudi Press Agency (SPA).

"The minister asserted that Iraq's return to exports...had only a very limited effect on the oil market," SPA late on Saturday reported Nuaimi as saying in Cairo after a meeting of the Organisation of Arab Petroleum Exporting Countries (OAPEC).
Under an oil-for-food deal agreed with the United Nations, Iraq will export between 500,000 and 600,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude at current prices.
The first tanker to load Iraqi oil for six years docked at the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan on Saturday.
"I think the (oil) prices are now good...The market now is improving," Nuaimi said.
North Sea Brent futures surged to $23.55 a barrel on Friday as prospects of colder temperatures prompted a buying spree which took prices $1 higher.
